page: Microsoft Azure D2_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz. The configuration includes 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. Memory capacity is 8.0 GB, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage is bundled with this instance, and it does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates moderate single-core capabilities but limited multi-core and memory throughput. The single-core stress-ng performance of 1427.09 and the Geekbench single-core score of 1218.0 both fall within the average tier. However, multi-core metrics are constrained, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 1466.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 1867.38, both placing in the bottom 10%. Memory performance is similarly restricted; read-only large block bandwidth is 12.96 GB/sec, and write large block bandwidth is 10.78 GB/sec.

Given the 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and the lack of local storage, this instance is positioned as an entry-level general-purpose resource. It is appropriate for lightweight workloads such as basic web serving, small-scale text processing, or simple single-threaded applications. It is not recommended for memory-intensive databases, parallelized compilation, or large-scale LLM inference, as demonstrated by its low scores in database operations and multi-threaded benchmarks.
